O.content: The title literally reads "Selected High-Growth Quarters: Ad Spend vs Sales".
Only five labeled markers, Q2 through Q6, are visible, and no full-period comparison, profitability measure, or decision threshold is visibly printed.

B.text: If a chart is explicitly limited to selected high-growth quarters and does not display the full campaign data or a decision threshold, then the chart alone is insufficient to establish that the observed association generalizes to a broader budget increase; request full-data analysis.
B.conditions: Applies when approval requires evidence beyond a selected subset, such as full-period performance, causal evidence, profitability, or risk review.

O.content: The title literally reads "Selected High-Growth Quarters: Ad Spend vs Sales".
The horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and shows ticks from 25 through 75.
The vertical-axis inscription reads "Sales ($ thousands)" and shows ticks from 50 through 170.
The blue markers labeled Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, and Q6 progress upward and to the right on the page.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, both in $ thousands, and the labeled quarter markers are the relevant evidence for a broader budget decision, then an upward-right pattern supports approving a broader budget increase; this assumes the selected quarters are representative and the association is sufficient for the decision.
B.conditions: Applies only if the displayed selected high-growth quarters are representative of the broader campaign context and no additional profitability, causality, or policy threshold is required.
